title: Lighting a votive candle
framing: guided, explanatory, no scores or win states
intro: A votive candle is lit before a statue, image or shrine as a private devotion. This walkthrough explains what happens and what the practice is understood to mean, from Catholic reference works. It is an explanation, not a prayer made on your behalf. Nothing is scored.

sources.cite: "Candles", The Catholic Encyclopedia, vol. 3 (New York: Robert Appleton, 1908). New Advent.

steps.text: Votive candles stand in racks before a statue, image or shrine of Christ, Mary or a saint.

steps.text: A candle is lit. The word "votive" comes from the Latin votum, a vow: the custom began as lighting a candle to fulfil a private vow.

steps.text: The candle is left to burn down before the image. In Catholic understanding it stands for the person's prayer and sacrifice, continuing after they have gone.
